steps.text: Click "Add" — OptimCE first asks how you want to build the new allocation key.
steps.title: Add a key

steps.text: Two ways of building a key are offered. Pick "Full editor" to type the iterations and percentages straight into the grid.
steps.title: Choose the mode

steps.text: Give the new allocation key a name and a description. This metadata appears in the key list and makes it easier to find later.
steps.title: Name the key

steps.text: Give the new allocation key a name and a description. This metadata appears in the key list and makes it easier to find later.
steps.title: Name the key

steps.text: Click "Add iteration" — the grid spawns a fresh iteration block with an initial consumer row ready to edit.
steps.title: Add an iteration

steps.text: Add one row per consumer of the key.
steps.title: Add a consumer

steps.text: Click "Add consumer" as many times as needed to reach the desired count — three rows in this scenario.
steps.title: Add consumers

steps.text: Set 70% of the energy for this iteration, name the three consumers (Cons1, Cons2, Cons3) and manually split the share 40/40/20.
steps.title: Configure the iteration

steps.text: Click "Add prorata iteration" — consumer names are carried over automatically and the percentages will be computed from actual consumption.
steps.title: Add a prorata iteration

steps.text: Type 30% as the weight of the second iteration so the two iterations together reach 100% of the energy.
steps.title: Set the weight

steps.text: As soon as the weight is committed (Enter or clicking outside the cell), the whole second iteration is recomputed automatically in prorata mode.
steps.title: Iteration recomputed

steps.text: Scan the full grid to confirm the iterations, names and percentages before saving the key.
steps.title: Review the configuration

steps.text: The new "E2E key" shows up in the community's allocation keys list, ready to be used by a sharing operation.
steps.title: Key created
